original_query: SELECT NAME, CAST(SUM(CN) FILTER (WHERE g_1) AS BIGINT), CAST(SUM(SM) FILTER (WHERE g_2) AS INTEGER) FROM (SELECT NAME, CN, SM, GROUPING(NAME, CN, SM) = 1 AS g_1, GROUPING(NAME, CN, SM) = 2 AS g_2 FROM (SELECT NAME, COUNT(*) AS CN, SUM(DEPTNO) AS SM FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME) AS t3 GROUP BY GROUPING SETS((NAME, CN), (NAME, SM))) AS t5 GROUP BY NAME
rewritten_query:
SELECT NAME, CAST(COUNT(*) AS BIGINT), CAST(SUM(DEPTNO) AS INTEGER)
FROM DEPT
GROUP BY NAME

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Collapse the three-level aggregation: the inner GROUP BY NAME already yields one row per NAME, so the GROUPING SETS and outer re-aggregation merely relay the same CN and SM values back per NAME. Replace the entire nested structure with a single GROUP BY NAME aggregation.
Since each NAME has exactly one CN row (g_1) and one SM row (g_2), the SUM(... FILTER ...) expressions are redundant; directly apply COUNT(*) and SUM(DEPTNO) with the target casts.
Remove the t3 and t5 subqueries and GROUPING flags entirely — no CTE is needed for this simple single-table aggregation.
